advances: A factorization of signed trace certificates with an explicit extra signed volume hypothesis for the new facets.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: The facets of $K_z\times B$ are precisely $F\times B$ with $F$ a facet of $K_z$, and $K_z\times G$ with $G$ a facet of $B$. This follows since a face exposed by a product linear functional is the product of the exposed faces in the factors, and the codimensions must sum to one. The shared inequalities are the old ones together with the facet inequalities of $B$, and the caps still depend only on $(z,x)$. The signed trace on an old plane is therefore $W_f\otimes(\mathcal L^k|_B)$, and on a new plane from $G$ it is $V\otimes(\mathcal H^{k-1}|_G)$. These equalities hold for Euclidean area because the factors are orthogonal. Each integral factors, and its first factor vanishes. Use $\psi=1$ for the mass and original first moments, and $a=1,\psi(w)=w_i$ on the compact $B$ for the new coordinate moments.

statement: Let finitely many full-dimensional polytopes $K_z\subset\mathbb R^m$ be fibers given by one shared plane list, with a unique owner at each facet, and let caps $H_j$ have no coincidence with any fiber facet. For coefficients $\lambda_j\ge0$, let $W_f$ be the objective boundary measure on the facets owned by $f$ minus $\sum_j\lambda_j$ times its restrictions to the caps. Keep the integer base label $z$ in this measure. Let $V$ be the summed fiber volume measure minus $\sum_j\lambda_j$ times its restrictions to the same caps. Suppose each $W_f$ and $V$ integrates every affine function of $(z,x)$ to zero. Replace each fiber by $K_z\times B$ for any full-dimensional compact polytope $B\subset\mathbb R^k$, $k\ge1$, and keep the caps independent of the new coordinate $w$. On every product shared plane the resulting signed boundary measure integrates every function $a(z,x)\psi(w)$ to zero for affine $a$ and bounded measurable $\psi$. In particular all its signed masses and full $(z,x,w)$ first moments vanish.
title: Tensorization of signed shared-plane facet moments
